Prune a Network's Edges

Source: R/prune.R
net_prune.Rd

net_prune() removes weak or non-significant edges from a network and returns the pruned network with a record of what it removed, so the pruning can be undone and re-applied. It is Nestimate's counterpart of tna::prune(); the net_ prefix avoids a name clash with it. It takes a netobject or a netobject_group, whose networks are pruned one by one with the same settings, and offers four methods (see Methods).

Pruning is non-destructive: the network carries a "pruning" attribute with the original weights, the pruned weights, the settings used and a table of the removed edges. net_deprune() restores the original weights and net_reprune() re-applies the pruning, both without recomputing anything; net_pruning_details() lists what was removed.

"threshold" and "lowest" remove small weights; they do not show that those edges are absent, and the cut-off is the analyst's choice. "disparity" and "bootstrap" keep an edge on a statistical criterion. Before reading a pruned network, see which edges went with net_pruning_details() and whether the conclusions hold at another cut-off; bootstrap_network() gives the uncertainty of each edge.

Usage

net_prune(
  x,
  method = "threshold",
  threshold = 0.1,
  lowest = 0.05,
  level = 0.5,
  boot = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'netobject'
net_prune(
  x,
  method = "threshold",
  threshold = 0.1,
  lowest = 0.05,
  level = 0.5,
  boot = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'netobject_group'
net_prune(
  x,
  method = "threshold",
  threshold = 0.1,
  lowest = 0.05,
  level = 0.5,
  boot = NULL,
  ...
)

# Default S3 method
net_prune(
  x,
  method = "threshold",
  threshold = 0.1,
  lowest = 0.05,
  level = 0.5,
  boot = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

The network: a netobject or a netobject_group. Another class raises an error. A network whose pruning is active raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input; after net_deprune() it can be pruned again with other settings, which replaces its pruning record.

method

The pruning method: "threshold" (default), "lowest", "disparity" or "bootstrap" (see Methods).

threshold

For method = "threshold": the largest weight that is removed. Default 0.1. Ignored by the other methods, but must still be a single number.

lowest

For method = "lowest": the quantile, between 0 and 1, of the positive weights that sets the cut-off. Default 0.05. Ignored by the other methods, but checked whatever the method: a value outside [0, 1] raises an error.

level

For method = "disparity": the significance level, between 0 and 1; an edge is kept when its p-value is below it. Default 0.5. Ignored by the other methods, but checked whatever the method: a value outside [0, 1] raises an error.

boot

For method = "bootstrap": a net_bootstrap from bootstrap_network() of this network. With the default NULL, the bootstrap is run here on x. For a netobject_group, pass the net_bootstrap_group of bootstrap_network() on the group, matched to the networks by name, or NULL to bootstrap each network on its own. Another object, a bootstrap of another network (its weights differ), a single net_bootstrap for a group, or a group bootstrap missing one of the networks raises an error of class nestimate_bad_input.

...

For method = "bootstrap" with boot = NULL: arguments passed to bootstrap_network(), such as iter. Ignored otherwise.

Value

The input, of the same class, with the pruned weights, its edge table and edge count updated to them, and the "pruning" attribute described above. net_pruning_details() reads the record, net_deprune() and net_reprune() switch between the original and the pruned weights. For a netobject_group, each network is pruned and carries its own record.

Methods

"threshold"

Removes positive edges with weight at most threshold.

"lowest"

Removes positive edges with weight at most the lowest quantile of the positive weights (self-loops included in the quantile; each pair counted once on an undirected network).

"disparity"

Keeps the backbone found by the disparity filter of Serrano, Boguna & Vespignani (2009): an edge stays when, at its source's outgoing or its target's incoming edges, its share of the strength is significant at level against a uniform split of that strength; the filter is defined for non-negative weights.

"bootstrap"

Removes the edges that bootstrap_network() finds non-significant: pass a computed result as boot, or bootstrap arguments through ....

For "threshold" and "lowest", the candidate edges are visited one at a time, column by column and down each column, and each is removed only when the network stays weakly connected without it, so a network that is not weakly connected to begin with loses no edge to these two methods. "disparity" and "bootstrap" apply no connectivity check. Negative edges are never candidates for "threshold" and "lowest", whatever their size. On a signed network, "disparity" treats negative edges as not significant and removes them at the default level; at a level above 0.5, a negative edge leaving a state with no positive outgoing edge (or entering one with no positive incoming edge) can stay. "bootstrap" removes the non-significant edges of either sign.

On an undirected network an edge is a pair of cells: it is removed in both directions or kept in both, so the pruned matrix stays symmetric, and the record lists and counts it once.

Self-loops (the diagonal) are observed data: they count towards the "lowest" quantile but are never removed by any method. This is a deliberate difference from tna::prune(), which prunes self-loops like any other edge.

References

Serrano, M. A., Boguna, M., & Vespignani, A. (2009). Extracting the multiscale backbone of complex weighted networks. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 106(16), 6483–6488. doi:10.1073/pnas.0808904106

See also

net_deprune, net_reprune, net_pruning_details

Examples

seqs <- data.frame(
  V1 = c("A","B","A","C","B"), V2 = c("B","C","B","A","C"),
  V3 = c("C","A","C","B","A"))
net    <- build_network(seqs, method = "relative")
pruned <- net_prune(net, method = "threshold", threshold = 0.2)
net_pruning_details(pruned)
#> Pruning details
#>   Method:  user-specified threshold (0.2)
#>   Removed: 0 edges
#>   Retained: 3 edges
#> 
#> (no edges removed)
